bio_en: Vahan Navasardian was born in Shushi in 1888, the son of a merchant poisoned in Turkestan, and was raised with his brother Hamest by their widowed mother; rebellious, he was expelled four times from Armenian and Russian schools. From his student years he wrote for almost all ARF papers. He taught at the Shushi diocesan school in 1913-14 and at the Gevorgian seminary from 1916, and at the end of 1917 became editor of Horizon in Tiflis, holding party posts in Etchmiadzin, Yerevan and Tiflis. In exile in Cairo he published many works on ARF ideology, Armenian independence and socialism, and he died in 1956.
